taxonomy_findings.detail: Q16 asks what a consumer does when price exceeds marginal utility for a single good. consumer.equilibrium's covers line states the equi-marginal rule only as a two-good comparison (MUa/Pa=MUb/Pb), while consumer.utility covers how MU explains the demand curve. Neither line names the single-good price-versus-MU adjustment that this kind of question actually tests, so it can be argued either way.

Q22 to Q24 read a diagram with only AC and AVC curves and ask for an 'equilibrium output'. costs.concepts covers defining and calculating cost figures from a table or function, not reading equilibrium off a curve; markets.perfect and markets.profit-shutdown both assume a price or marginal revenue line is shown, which this diagram does not have. There is no subtopic for finding a firm's optimum or equilibrium output from cost curves alone, without a stated market structure or revenue line.
